mcqs.q: Which is a DIGITAL image receptor?
mcqs.explain: Digital receptors are solid-state (CCD, CMOS) and photostimulable phosphor (PSP) plates; films are analogue receptors.

mcqs.q: Direct-action (non-screen) film is sensitive primarily to:
mcqs.explain: Direct-action (non-screen/packet) film is exposed mainly by x-ray photons; screen film is exposed mainly by light from intensifying screens.

mcqs.q: Indirect-action (screen) film, used in a cassette, is sensitive primarily to:
opts: Light emitted by the adjacent intensifying screens
mcqs.explain: Screen film responds mainly to the light from the intensifying screens, which greatly reduces the patient dose (used extra-orally).

mcqs.q: Which intra-oral film size is the OCCLUSAL film?
mcqs.explain: Sizes: #0 child, #1 narrow anterior, #2 adult, #3 bitewing, #4 occlusal.

mcqs.q: The four basic components of a radiographic film are:
opts: Plastic base, adhesive, emulsion and protective gelatin layer
mcqs.explain: Film = plastic base + adhesive + emulsion (both sides) + a protective clear-gelatin layer.

mcqs.q: The plastic base of radiographic film is made of cellulose acetate and:
opts: Supports the emulsion but does not contribute to the final image
mcqs.explain: The clear cellulose-acetate base is only a support for the emulsion; it plays no part in forming the image.

mcqs.q: The light-sensitive emulsion of dental film is coated:
opts: On both sides of the base
mcqs.explain: The silver-halide emulsion is applied to both sides of the base, with a protective gelatin layer over each.

mcqs.q: The CCD, introduced to dentistry in 1987, was:
opts: The first digital image receptor adapted for intra-oral imaging
mcqs.explain: The charge-coupled device (CCD), introduced in 1987, was the first digital receptor adapted for intra-oral imaging — a silicon-crystal pixel matrix.

mcqs.q: Because CCDs are more sensitive to light than to x-rays, they are coated with:
mcqs.explain: A scintillator (gadolinium oxybromide) is coated on the CCD to convert x-rays into light that the silicon detects.

mcqs.q: A CMOS sensor differs from a CCD mainly in that:
opts: Each pixel is isolated and directly connected to its own transistor
It is exposed only to sound waves
mcqs.explain: Both are silicon-based, but in CMOS each pixel is isolated and connected directly to a transistor, changing how the charge is read out.

mcqs.q: Flat-panel detectors use the photoconductor selenium and are mainly used for:
mcqs.explain: Selenium flat-panel detectors are relatively expensive and currently limited to specialised tasks such as CBCT.

mcqs.q: A PSP plate stores x-ray energy and releases it as light when stimulated; its material is:
mcqs.explain: PSP imaging uses europium-doped barium fluorohalide, which absorbs/stores x-ray energy and releases it as light (phosphorescence) when laser-scanned.

mcqs.q: The 'latent image' in DIGITAL imaging is formed as:
opts: Electrical charges later converted to a digital signal
A chemical change in the emulsion
mcqs.explain: In digital receptors the latent image is electrical charge; in analogue film it is a chemical change that becomes visible after processing.

mcqs.q: During film processing, the DEVELOPER:
opts: Reduces the exposed silver-halide crystals to black metallic silver
mcqs.explain: The developer reduces the exposed silver-halide grains to black metallic silver, producing the dark areas of the image.

mcqs.q: The FIXER in film processing:
opts: Removes the unexposed silver-halide crystals and hardens the emulsion
Reduces exposed crystals to black silver
mcqs.explain: The fixer dissolves away the unexposed/undeveloped crystals (clearing the film) and hardens the emulsion, before washing and drying.

mcqs.q: The two variants of MANUAL (wet) film processing are:
mcqs.explain: Manual processing uses either the (preferred) time-temperature method or the visual method; other approaches are automatic and self-developing films.

mcqs.q: A darkroom for manual processing must above all be:
mcqs.explain: Absolute light-tightness is essential so that only the safelight (not white light) reaches the unwrapped film.

mcqs.q: Darkroom safelights should be positioned and rated:
opts: ~1.2 m (4 ft) from the work surface, 25 W, with a suitable filter
mcqs.explain: Safelights are placed ~1.2 m (4 ft) from the work surface, use 25 W bulbs and a filter matched to the film type.

mcqs.q: Used lead foil pieces from film packets should be:
opts: Recycled — never thrown in the trash
mcqs.explain: Lead foil must be collected in a recycle container; it should not be discarded in the regular trash.

mcqs.q: Which piece of equipment is part of a MANUAL processing setup?
opts: Solution tanks, thermometer, immersion heater, timer and film hangers
mcqs.explain: Manual processing uses tanks of solutions, a thermometer, immersion heater, an accurate timer and film hangers.

mcqs.q: Adjusting brightness/contrast, sharpening and smoothing an image are examples of:
mcqs.explain: Digital image processing includes restoration, enhancement, brightness/contrast adjustment, and sharpening/smoothing.

mcqs.q: Compared with film, an advantage of solid-state digital sensors is:
opts: Immediate image with no chemical processing, and post-capture manipulation
mcqs.explain: Digital sensors give an instant image (no wet chemistry/darkroom) that can be enhanced, and generally use less dose than film.

saqs.q: Classify image receptors with an example of each class.
saqs.a: Analogue: direct-action (non-screen) & indirect-action (screen) film. Digital: solid-state (CCD, CMOS) & photostimulable phosphor (PSP) plate.

saqs.q: List the four components of radiographic film and the role of the base.
saqs.a: Plastic base (cellulose acetate — support only, no image), adhesive, emulsion (both sides), protective gelatin layer.

saqs.q: Give the five intra-oral film sizes.
saqs.a: #0 child, #1 narrow anterior, #2 adult, #3 bitewing, #4 occlusal.

saqs.q: Describe how a CCD detector works and why it needs a scintillator.
saqs.a: A CCD is a silicon-crystal pixel matrix (1987, first intra-oral digital receptor). It is more sensitive to light than x-rays, so a scintillator (gadolinium oxybromide) is coated on it to convert x-rays into light.

saqs.q: State the functions of the developer and the fixer.
saqs.a: Developer: reduces exposed silver-halide to black metallic silver (dark image). Fixer: removes unexposed crystals and hardens the emulsion.

saqs.q: How is a PSP plate's latent image read, and what is the plate made of?
saqs.a: The plate (europium-doped barium fluorohalide) stores x-ray energy; when scanned by laser light it releases the energy as light (phosphorescence), which is digitized.

saqs.q: List the key requirements of a processing darkroom.
saqs.a: Absolute light-tightness, adequate washing, infection control, biohazard & lead-foil recycle containers, white light, and safelights (4 ft, 25 W, correct filter).
